recommendation: Keep the source change. It restores the final FHIR-I clarification at the relevant terminology anchors without deciding later Triaged typo issue FHIR-50604.
issue_request: FHIR-31385 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested paragraphs in the required and extensible binding-strength sections clarifying that data-absent-reason or other extensions do not bypass binding requirements.
initial_application: Commit 3946ca05fe initially applied the issue by adding a required-binding paragraph to source/terminologies.html and related primitive-extension prose to source/extensibility.html. The requested extensible paragraph was not added to terminologies.html, and the next-day batch commit ab0ada5222 removed the required paragraph from terminologies.html while applying unrelated terminology issues.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively identifies the terminologies module with resourceType=terminologies, making source/terminologies.html current build source. Current source/extensibility.html still contains related extension guidance, but the authoritative terminologies.html#required and terminologies.html#extensible sections lacked the Jira-approved clarification. FHIR-I Confluence minutes confirm the persuasive vote, and Zulip discussion around US Core missing-data guidance links FHIR-31385 as the base spec tracker for this confusion.
reconciliation: Added the required-binding extension-bypass paragraph and the missing extensible-binding data-absent-reason example to source/terminologies.html using the current data-absent-reason extension link macro.
source_changes: source/terminologies.html: added explicit required-binding guidance that data-absent-reason or other extensions cannot satisfy a required binding.
source/terminologies.html: added explicit extensible-binding guidance that data-absent-reason cannot replace an applicable in-value-set concept such as unknown.

related_jiras.note: Later Triaged R6 typo report for the existing extensibility.html wording; not final and not decided in this reconciliation.
